chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan, from Fadalah, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said: 'I miss the Witr prayer in the morning until night; how should I make it up?' He said: 'Like for like.'
As for what has been narrated that he makes it up as an even number (shaf') if he makes it up after Dhuhr, that is like what was narrated.
ai.seo_question: How should the Witr prayer be made up if missed?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the primary Shia ruling that the Witr prayer is a single rak'ah to be made up individually ('like for like'), distinguishing it from the Sunni practice of treating it as an even number. The text acknowledges a secondary view where Witr is made up as an even number if performed after Dhuhr, reflecting the scholarly nuance between its status as a confirmed Sunnah versus a distinct prayer. This highlights the jurisprudential flexibility within the school of Ahl al-Bayt regarding the timing and structure of making up this specific prayer.
